scope: Eight reviewed evidence-boundary answers, not additional SQL module review.

help_topics.title: Understanding permissions and personal configuration
help_topics.business_question: Can this help show another user’s effective work configuration?
help_topics.plain_answer: This help library explains general work-selection rules. It does not access individual users, permissions or effective profiles. A colleague’s settings cannot be inferred from configuration totals or from the parameters a procedure accepts.
input_context: The named setting or process, relevant warehouse/profile scope and observation date.

execution_steps.explanation: Work selection accepts a user and warehouse and applies profile and sequence rules.
The retained configuration checks aggregate fixed fields. They do not identify the profile applied to an individual operator.

configuration_dependencies: User, warehouse, profile, sequence and feature settings can change the work-selection path.
explanation_paths: For an individual access problem, use an authorized, sanitized explanation of the relevant permission/profile and application binding; do not provide another person’s operational data.
boundaries: No user-specific permission decision or access-control result is established by this prototype.

cases.question: Why can’t aggregate profile totals tell me which rules a colleague uses?
must_explain: Explain the distinction between general rules, aggregate evidence and a specific user.
must_not_claim: Disclose or guess a colleague profile or permission.

help_topics.title: Handling missing locating settings
help_topics.business_question: What happens if a locating setting is missing?
help_topics.plain_answer: Missing locating settings have no universal SCALE fallback. The result depends on the exact rule, assignment and receiving preference.
input_context: The named setting or process, relevant warehouse/profile scope and observation date.

execution_steps.explanation: Locating selects a storage destination through a rule and strategy.
Inspect the missing-value branch for the selected setting; the introductory locating passage does not define every case.

configuration_dependencies: The documented delayed-locating path requires both Delayed Locating and Create Putaway Work.
explanation_paths: Identify the rule, item or rule-set assignment and receiving preference, then check the missing-value behavior for that exact setting.
boundaries: An absent setting must not be treated as enabled, disabled or first-match without its specific fallback definition.

cases.question: Does an absent locating flag automatically mean delayed locating is enabled?
must_explain: Explain the two-flag dependency and unresolved specific missing-setting behavior.
must_not_claim: Assume that a missing value enables locating.

help_topics.title: Configuration precedence and overlapping rules
help_topics.business_question: Two profile or rule rows seem to apply. Which one wins?
help_topics.plain_answer: The winner depends on the exact query or application rule. In the reviewed work selector, some options use profile alone and others also use sequence. Do not assume that the first displayed row wins or that a primary key on an unrelated field makes the selection unique.
input_context: The named setting or process, relevant warehouse/profile scope and observation date.

execution_steps.explanation: Identify the statement and its actual profile, sequence, warehouse and user filters.
Inspect its ordering, uniqueness constraints and fallback. Where no unique ordering is established, retain the selection ambiguity.

configuration_dependencies: Changing sequence scope can change which rows qualify. Different routines can use different precedence.
explanation_paths: Compare only the needed sanitized keys and the applicable rule’s ordering; do not execute the work selector as a read-only diagnostic because a branch changes instruction sequence.
boundaries: This explains an ambiguity to check; it does not establish that duplicate rows exist here.

cases.question: Does the first row shown on a configuration screen always take precedence?
must_explain: Explain exact-query scope, ordering and possible ties.

help_topics.title: What retained configuration checks can tell you
help_topics.business_question: Do the retained checks prove today’s effective settings?
help_topics.plain_answer: Five retained configuration checks describe aggregate fields observed on 29 September 2026 at 22:50:28-30 UTC. They do not identify an individual user's effective preference or a particular action's outcome.
input_context: The named setting or process, relevant warehouse/profile scope and observation date.

execution_steps.explanation: Match the requested setting to the check's recorded scope and observation time.
Use profile assignment and sequence precedence to determine which configuration applies to a particular user.

explanation_paths: For a user-specific question, check the assigned profile or preference and its selection sequence.

cases.question: Can yesterday’s configuration snapshot guarantee my setting now?
must_explain: State owner-attested current baseline, retained timestamp and aggregate-versus-user scope.
must_not_claim: Guarantee current primary or per-user settings.

help_topics.title: Design revisions and release applicability
help_topics.business_question: What does a reference document establish about release applicability?
help_topics.plain_answer: A design revision, training date or printed date does not establish the release or configuration of an installed SCALE system. The functionality reference explains documented mechanisms with local limits. Example values, proposed extensions and unresolved comments do not become universal defaults or deployed behavior.
help_topics.trigger: Distinguishing a document revision or training date from supported product behavior.
input_context: The named workflow or setting and the scope of the question.

execution_steps.explanation: Use the relevant functionality entry and its supporting source locations.
Keep release dependencies, configuration choices and unresolved limitations attached to the explanation.
An implementation example does not establish an active setting or prove that a feature is enabled in the current workflow.

configuration_dependencies: Release support, effective configuration and design revision are separate facts.
boundaries: Design examples and proposed extensions do not establish installed functionality.

help_topics.title: Understanding cycle-count tolerance and review
help_topics.business_question: Is our cycle-count tolerance zero or 9999?
help_topics.plain_answer: Cycle-count verification can require two consecutive equal counts. Counts outside the applicable tolerance can move to Pending Review for reconciliation.
input_context: The named workflow or setting and the scope of the question.

execution_steps.explanation: Verify Bad Count repeats a discrepant count; two consecutive equal counts establish the reported quantity in the described workflow.
Counts outside the user's tolerance move to Pending Review. An authorized reviewer reconciles the correct on-hand quantity and closes the request.
Check whether a separate plan-closing restriction applies to this workflow.

configuration_dependencies: Establish tolerance units, scope and recount/reconciliation permissions for the applicable configuration.
boundaries: Example values such as 0 or 9999 do not define a universal default or the active warehouse tolerance.
The recorded restriction on closing an entire plan is a separate extension, not base behavior.

cases.question: Does a cycle-count example establish our active tolerance and review rules?
must_explain: Separate count verification, configured tolerance and reconciliation; current settings are not established.
must_not_claim: Select zero or 9999 as the active setting.

help_topics.title: Understanding wave duration and statement timing
help_topics.business_question: How long does an entire wave take?
help_topics.plain_answer: The retained Query Store evidence cannot answer the whole-wave duration. It contains statement statistics for 163 historical object IDs. A statement can execute several times inside a procedure, and a wave can include application, queue, database and external stages. Statement counts are not procedure-call counts.
input_context: The named setting or process, relevant warehouse/profile scope and observation date.

execution_steps.explanation: Keep object, replica group, execution type and retained interval dimensions with statement statistics.
A weighted mean combines recorded statement executions; it is not a start-to-finish wave time or a sum of all application stages.
A process measurement requires correlated start/end events, stage boundaries, retries and completion acknowledgment across the involved components.

configuration_dependencies: Queue delay, configuration choices, asynchronous work, retries and external completion can fall outside SQL statement measurements.
explanation_paths: Use a sanitized event-schema example with correlation ID and UTC stage start/end semantics, plus observation time and process scope. Do not execute warehouse work to manufacture a timing result.
boundaries: Current object-name matches do not establish the historical definition used by Query Store. Missing history does not prove a routine is unused. No continuous interval coverage is assumed.

cases.question: Can I add SQL statement averages to get the full wave time?
must_explain: Separate weighted statement averages from correlated process duration.
must_not_claim: Report Query Store counts as calls or complete elapsed time.

help_topics.title: Checking label prerequisites before assuming print success
help_topics.business_question: Does selecting a document prove the label printed?
help_topics.plain_answer: A label needs a definition, document type, document association and output route. Setup depends on the intended business event and printing path.
input_context: The named workflow or setting and the scope of the question.

execution_steps.explanation: Identify the label file, document type, document definition and output routing for the intended business event.
Some labels use a stored procedure. Wave-driven output may require the Documents and Labels step.
Check printer capability against the label definition and actual device. A returned document choice does not establish physical output.

boundaries: Mixed-release training does not establish installed printer capability or a complete setup sequence for every label.

cases.question: Does the training deck prove our installed printer supports this label?
must_explain: Explain documented prerequisites and missing installed/output evidence.
must_not_claim: Claim verified printer support or physical output.

prior_revision.scope: Prior integration manifest before synchronization to the central functionality reference.
